title: The Devil Standing at the Right Hand
english: A light cloud is assigned to bring the evangelical rain upon the fruitful crops and to shield from the heat from which the prudent man is saved, according to the proverbial decree: 'A prudent son was saved from the heat.' It also shields from the frost of sin, as it is written: 'As a pit chills water, so its wickedness chills.' To this, one will take allegorically: 'A cold north wind shall blow.'

Taking these things said according to contemplation, having possessed fleshy hearts that resembled God's judgments and commands, we might have been reverent toward God so that we might do right, so that God, benefiting the flesh even more, might engrave a divine writing in them with His living Spirit, not as stones, by which we might be helped to be perfected so as to face face to face with the truth, surpassing the seeing of it iconically and in part.
And the Lord showed me Joshua the high priest standing before the face of an angel of the Lord, and the devil stood at his right hand to oppose him (Zech 3:1).

But God shows great and superlative things that happen, which are neither sensible nor human. Because of this, God shows to the prophet the great priest Joshua not standing humanly, but standing divinely before the face of an angel of the Lord; not merely the son of Josedech as is shown through him, but the truly great priest, having traversed the heavens, the one ordained 'according to the order of Melchizedek,' not according to the power of a fleshy commandment for a certain time, but according to an unpassable priesthood; for it has been said of him: 'You are a priest forever' (Ps 110:4). Jesus the great priest was not shown merely as it happened, but standing unshakeable and firmly established, similarly to what was said in the Gospel: 'Jesus cried out saying: If anyone thirsts, let him come to me and drink' (John 7:37).

For everyone coming to him drinks, because he stands ready. Regarding the one standing, he is seen by God in the presence of an angel of the Lord, and the devil was seen standing at his right hand to oppose him. For what was necessary for the devil to oppose and stand against, if not the right hands of the one shown by the Lord, standing in addition to the angel of the great counsel?

And he stood also at the right hand of Judas, as it is said in the 108th Psalm: 'Set the sinner against him, and let the devil stand at his right hand.' But see the great difference in the words; for regarding the one betraying the Savior, he stands at the right hands having already taken them, 'having given place to the devil.' For it is said that 'he cast into his heart to betray' the one who had chosen him as best teacher and also Savior. And after the casting into the heart, he had entered into him in order to work the things of betrayal in him as he works in the children of disobedience. For it is written that 'after the morsel Satan entered into him.'

But the great priest did not stand at the right hands any other way than by opposing him, especially when he attempts to seize those being helped and instructed by him; does he not stand opposing from the right hands when he seeks to exclude those called to faith and the rest of virtue, according to what was said: 'Behold, Satan has asked of you to sift you like wheat, and I have prayed for you,' O Peter, our disciple, 'so that your faith may not fail' (Luke 22:31)?

Regarding not being harmed by those whom he opposes, and they receive authority against him, so that they tread upon all the power of the one opposing hostily, they suffer no harm at all because of hoping in the one who is being crushed under the feet of the saints, the standing and muddy devil; for it is written: 'Everyone having hope in God' (Romans 15:13) will remain without infirmity and undefeated, not fainting, not falling away.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.
